name: Ángel Di María
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal with Argentina at the 2008 Beijing Olympics at age 20, scoring the winning goal in the final against Nigeria.
early_history_summary: Di María joined Rosario Central's youth system at age four and made his professional debut at 17 in December 2005. He won the FIFA U-20 World Cup with Argentina in 2007 and signed for Benfica at 19, where he won the Primeira Liga before moving to Real Madrid at 22.
family_context_summary: Born into poverty in Rosario, Argentina; father Miguel worked in a coal yard for 16 years and mother Diana took Ángel to training by bicycle; the family struggled to afford football boots.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Miguel nearly made it to River Plate's first team but suffered a serious knee injury; he later supported Ángel's football development and gave up his job when Ángel signed for Benfica.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, coal yard work, father's football background, Rosario Central academy, Argentine football pipeline
evidence_summary: Born into poverty in Rosario, Argentina, Di María began playing football at age three on a doctor's recommendation for his hyperactivity, joining Rosario Central's youth system at four. His father Miguel worked in a coal yard for 16 years and had nearly made it to River Plate's first team before a knee injury; Di María helped deliver coal from age 10. He made his professional debut at 17, won the U20 World Cup at 19, and signed for Benfica, where his father gave up his job to accompany him. He won Olympic gold with Argentina at the 2008 Beijing Olympics at age 20, scoring the winning goal in the final. His path was driven by physical talent, family sacrifice, and the Argentine football pipeline rather than inherited wealth or networks.
starting_point: Born into a poor family in Rosario, Argentina; father worked in a coal yard and mother was a homemaker who cycled him to football training.
current_position: Returned to Rosario Central in 2025 after 18 years in European football; won the 2022 FIFA World Cup with Argentina; estimated net worth ~$20M.

name: Apasra Hongsakula
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss Universe 1965 in Miami Beach at age 18, becoming the first Thai and first Southeast Asian to win the title.
early_history_summary: Born in Bangkok and sent to an English-language school in Penang, Malaysia, Apasra won the Miss Thailand pageant at age 17 in 1964 and was crowned Miss Universe in July 1965 at age 18.
family_context_summary: Born in Bangkok to Group Captain Perm and Kayoon Hongsakula; raised in a middle-class military family and sent to an English-language school in Penang.
primary_early_advantage_tags: military family, English education, pageant pipeline, Queen Sirikit mentorship
evidence_summary: Born in Bangkok to Group Captain Perm Hongsakula and Kayoon Hongsakula, Apasra was sent to learn English at a girls' secondary school in Penang, Malaysia. She won Miss Thailand at age 17 in 1964 and was crowned Miss Universe in July 1965 at age 18, becoming the first Thai and first Southeast Asian to win the title. Her military family background provided access to education and social connections, including reportedly receiving poise and presentation advice from Queen Sirikit before the pageant. Her milestone was achieved through physical beauty and presentation rather than sustained domain practice.
starting_point: Born in Bangkok to a military family; father was a Group Captain in the Thai Air Force; sent to English-language school in Penang.
current_position: Living privately in Thailand as a businesswoman; former Miss Universe 1965; age 78.

name: Magnus Lindberg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the UNESCO International Rostrum of Composers prize in 1982 at age 24 for '...de Tartuffe, je crois' (1981), marking his international breakthrough as a composer.
early_history_summary: Lindberg began piano at age 11 and entered the Sibelius Academy junior department at 15, studying composition under Rautavaara and Heininen. In 1977, at 19, he co-founded the Ears Open Society with Saariaho and Salonen, and in 1980 founded the Toimii Ensemble. His compositional breakthrough came with 'Action-Situation-Signification' in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Helsinki; father was a computer engineer. Started piano at age 11 and entered the Sibelius Academy junior department at 15.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sibelius Academy, Ears Open Society, Toimii Ensemble, avant-garde mentors, Helsinki
evidence_summary: Born in Helsinki to a computer engineer father, Lindberg began piano at age 11 and entered the Sibelius Academy's junior department at 15, studying composition under Rautavaara and Heininen. In 1977, at age 19, he co-founded the Ears Open Society with contemporaries including Kaija Saariaho and Esa-Pekka Salonen, and in 1980 founded the Toimii Ensemble. His compositional breakthrough came with 'Action-Situation-Signification' in 1982, which won the UNESCO International Rostrum of Composers prize that year at age 24. He benefited from Finland's elite composition education pipeline, sustained mentorship from leading avant-garde composers, and a high-trust peer network of young Finnish musicians.
starting_point: Born in Helsinki, Finland; father was a computer engineer; started piano at age 11.
current_position: Active composer; former composer-in-residence at NY Philharmonic (2009-2012) and London Philharmonic Orchestra (2014-2017); based in Helsinki.

Signed by SK Telecom T1 in February 2013 at age 16, he won the Korean championship and the Season 3 World Championship in his rookie year at age 17.

evidence_summary: Born in Seoul's Gangseo district to a financially struggling family, Lee Sang-hyeok began playing League of Legends at age 15 in 2011, quickly rising to the top of the Korean solo queue rankings under the name GoJeonPa. His father, a carpenter who had divorced his mother, supported his decision to drop out of high school and pursue esports professionally. Signed by SK Telecom T1 in February 2013 at age 16, Faker won the Season 3 World Championship in 2013 at age 17, defeating Royal Club 3-0 in the final in Los Angeles. His unprecedented mechanical skill and game intelligence, honed through thousands of hours of online play in South Korea's competitive gaming ecosystem, made him an instant superstar.

name: Antti Hyvärinen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in ski jumping at the 1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics at age 24, becoming the first non-Norwegian to win Olympic gold in ski jumping.
early_history_summary: Born in Rovaniemi, Finland, Hyvärinen was introduced to ski jumping at the Ounasvaara hill during the Continuation War winters. He made his international debut at the 1952 Oslo Olympics at age 20 (7th place), won the Finnish Championships in 1954, and won Olympic gold in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born in Rovaniemi, Finland; introduced to ski jumping at the Ounasvaara hill during the Continuation War winters as a child.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Rovaniemi, Ounasvaara hill, ski jumping culture, wartime childhood
evidence_summary: Born in Rovaniemi, Finland, Hyvärinen was introduced to ski jumping during the Continuation War winters at the Ounasvaara hill. He made his international debut at the 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo at age 20, finishing seventh. He won the Finnish Championships title in 1954 at age 22 and achieved his defining milestone at the 1956 Winter Olympics in Cortina d'Ampezzo, winning gold at age 24 to become the first non-Norwegian Olympic ski jumping champion. His career was cut short by a hip injury in 1957, after which he coached the Finnish national team from 1960 to 1964.

current_position: Died in 2000 at age 67 in Bad Nauheim, Germany; final role: former head coach of Finnish ski jumping team (1960-1964).

name: Marc Girardelli
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Cup overall title in 1985 at age 22 with 11 race victories, establishing himself as the dominant alpine skier of his era.
early_history_summary: Born in Lustenau, Austria, Girardelli started skiing at 5 and racing at 7, coached by his father Helmut. He won the Topolino race at 11, switched to Luxembourg at 13 after disputes with the Austrian federation, made his World Cup debut at 17, and won his first World Cup race at 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Lustenau, Austria into a family originally from Valsugana, Italy; father Helmut was a hotel owner who coached Marc from age five and managed his career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Helmut Girardelli was Marc's personal coach, training him with his own techniques and managing his career, including the decision to switch from Austria to Luxembourg.

evidence_summary: Born in Lustenau, Austria, Girardelli started skiing at age five and was racing at seven, coached by his father Helmut, a hotel owner who trained him with his own techniques. At 11, he won the Topolino race, the top international competition for young skiers. After disputes with the Austrian ski federation over coaching, he switched to representing Luxembourg at age 13, competing with a mini-team of just his father and a service man. He made his World Cup debut at 17 in 1980, achieved his first podium at 18, his first victory at 19, and won his first World Cup overall title at 22 in 1985, becoming one of the greatest alpine skiers in history.

current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 1996; became an entrepreneur involved in hotels, indoor ski slopes, and clothing; based in Luxembourg.

name: Sadaharu Oh

early_history_summary: Born in Tokyo to a Chinese immigrant father who ran a noodle shop, Oh was a star pitcher at Waseda High School and signed with the Yomiuri Giants in 1959 at 19. After a poor rookie season, batting coach Hiroshi Arakawa helped him develop his flamingo stance in 1962, and Oh led the league in home runs that year at 22.

evidence_summary: Born in Tokyo to a Chinese immigrant father who ran a noodle shop and a Japanese mother, Oh grew up in modest circumstances during and after World War II. He was a star pitcher at Waseda High School, leading his team to the Koshien championship, and signed with the Yomiuri Giants in 1959 at age 19. After a poor rookie season, batting coach Hiroshi Arakawa helped him develop his distinctive 'flamingo' batting stance in 1962, and Oh led the Central League in home runs that year at age 22. In 1964 at age 24, he broke the NPB single-season home run record with 55 and won the Central League MVP, establishing himself as Japan's premier slugger.

evidence_summary: Born Lorne Lipowitz in Toronto to a furrier father, Michaels grew up around his grandparents' movie house and began performing comedy at the University of Toronto, co-writing the U.C. Follies revue in 1963. He partnered with Hart Pomerantz, and the duo wrote for CBC Radio before moving to Los Angeles in 1968 to write for Laugh-In and The Beautiful Phyllis Diller Show. He studied at the Tallinn Music School and Conservatory under Gustav Ernesaks, then at the Leningrad Conservatory under Nikolai Rabinovitch. He joined the Estonian State Symphony Orchestra as a percussionist in 1959 at age 20 and made his conducting debut at the Estonian National Opera in 1964 at age 25 with Bernstein's West Side Story. He became a full-time conductor there in 1965 at age 26, launching a career that would span over 100 orchestras across 40 countries.
